mem.t: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

lessons.title: The Fall of the Shining One
lessons.theme: Satan’s very nature is the proud desire to be equal with God

v: How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of the dawn! How you are cut down to the ground, who laid the nations low!
You said in your heart, “I will ascend into heaven! I will exalt my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain of assembly, in the far north!
I will ascend above the heights of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!”

lessons.still: Quietly acknowledge: “Lord, spiritual warfare is real, but you have already won.” Hand your fears to the Lord, and ask him for a sober mind to see through the enemy’s schemes, without ever making the enemy bigger than the Lord.
teach: To treat an illness, a doctor must first identify what is causing it; get the cause wrong, and even the best medicine won’t help. Many of the symptoms in our spiritual lives—quarrels, bitterness, anxiety, self-indulgence—often have the same underlying cause: pride. To overcome, we must first recognise the original form of this disease.

Isaiah describes the arrogance of the king of Babylon, and in it we glimpse the proud spirit behind him: five times he says “I will”—I will ascend into heaven, I will exalt my throne, I will sit on the mountain of assembly, I will ascend above the clouds, I will make myself like the Most High. This is the prototype of self-rule: a creature trying to seize the Creator’s place. And it ends with “How you have fallen from heaven!”

When that ancient serpent said to humanity in Eden, “You will be like God,” he was passing his own disease on to us. So the heart of spiritual warfare is not mysterious phenomena but the battle over “who reigns.” Every time I insist on “I will,” I am in tune with the enemy; every time I say “What you desire,” I am standing on God’s side.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride is leaving our place and grasping power—and Satan was the first to do it. Self-rule is Satan’s nature; the self-emptied life is Christ’s nature. Once we see this clearly, we understand why humility overcomes pride, and the self-emptied life overcomes Satan.
q: Who is God? — God brings the proud one “fallen from heaven”; what does this reveal about his justice and sovereignty?
Who am I? — Which “I will”s in your life actually sound like the enemy’s voice?
How shall I respond? — Which “I will” will you change into “What you desire” today?
lessons.jesus: The enemy said, “I will ascend into heaven,” but Jesus came down from heaven. The enemy wanted to be equal with God, but Jesus “didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped.” The two roads are complete opposites: one climbs upward and falls; the other goes downward and is exalted to the highest place. Following Jesus means taking the downward road.
lessons.pray: Lord, I see the root of pride, and I see the “I will” that so often fills my heart. Forgive me for the times I have been in tune with the enemy. I don’t want to climb up high to be equal with you; I want to follow Jesus on the downward road. Keep me, so that I overcome in the place you have set for me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down three “I will”s you have said this week, and hand each one to the Lord
When a quarrel arises today, first ask: “Whose voice is this?”
Read Isaiah 14:12–15 and pray over your own heart
lessons.noon: “I will make myself like the Most High!” — Lord, right now I will not exalt myself; I want only you to be God.

lessons.title: The Cycle of Biting and Devouring
lessons.theme: Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose

v: Pride only breeds quarrels, but wisdom is with people who take advice.
But if you bite and devour one another, be careful that you don’t consume one another.

lessons.still: Think back to your most recent conflict. Don’t analyse who was right or wrong; simply look, in the Lord’s presence, at what your own heart was like at the time. Quietly ask, “Lord, back then, did I want to win, or did I want to love?”
teach: Two goats meet in the middle of a narrow log bridge. Neither will give way; they butt horns back and forth until both tumble into the river. Proud conflicts go just like that: you get louder, I get louder still; you go cold, I go colder. Each person feels they are only “responding,” and together they fall into the river.

Proverbs says, “Pride only breeds quarrels.” The root of an argument is often not the issue itself but the heart that says, “I can’t lose.” Paul warned the Galatian church: “If you bite and devour one another, be careful that you don’t consume one another.” James goes straight to the root: fights and quarrels come from the desires that battle within us. Pride provokes pride, and in the end there is no winner.

The key to breaking the cycle is to see clearly our own role in it. Rather than waiting for the other person to change first, ask: “Are my words putting out the fire, or adding fuel?” Deal with your own pride first—not because you must be the one in the wrong, but because you are the only party you can control.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility inspires humility and brings a win for everyone. The focus is not on others’ faults but on my own heart. People matter more than things; don’t hurt a person just to win an argument.
q: Who is God? — When God sees his children “biting and devouring” one another, what is his heart like?
Who am I? — In conflict, what is your most common way of “adding fuel”?
How shall I respond? — In which tense relationship will you be the first to stop trying to win?
lessons.jesus: All along the road the disciples argued about who was the greatest. Jesus did not join the argument; instead he called a little child to stand among them and taught them what true greatness is. When he was insulted, he did not insult in return; when he suffered, he made no threats. By refusing to strike back, he broke the cycle of pride.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that in conflict I often want to win and answer pride with pride, hurting others and myself. Forgive my biting and devouring words. Give me the courage to be the first to stop, the first to let go, the first to cool things down. In every relationship, make me someone who puts out fires, not someone who adds fuel. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Before speaking today, ask: “Will this put out the fire or add fuel?”
With someone you have recently clashed with, drop one point you “must win”
When you feel offended, silently count to ten and pray to the Lord
lessons.noon: “Pride only breeds quarrels.” — Lord, right now I lay down my need to win.

lessons.title: Jacob and Esau
lessons.theme: Humility inspires humility, and relationships become a win for both

v: He himself passed over in front of them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.
Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.
A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

lessons.still: Think of someone with whom there is distance between you. Quietly, before the Lord, speak one sentence of blessing over them. Then ask the Lord to show you a way to take one small, humble step towards them.
teach: A hammer cannot break through a frozen lake, but the sun can slowly melt it. The walls of ice between people are the same: meeting force with force only sends shards flying, but gentleness and humility can turn hard ice into flowing water.

Jacob had once cheated his brother out of his blessing. Twenty years later, on his way home, he heard that Esau was coming to meet him with four hundred men, and he trembled with fear. At the ford of the Jabbok he wrestled with God; he came away limping, and his life was changed. When he met his brother, he no longer played tricks; instead he bowed to the ground seven times. And Esau ran to embrace him, and they both wept. Proverbs says, “A gentle answer turns away wrath.”

Humility does not guarantee that the other person will change immediately, but it changes the atmosphere and gives the other person a way to step down gracefully. Pride leaves both sides with no way to back down; humility gives both sides a way forward. Spiritual victory is not “I win, you lose,” but God receiving glory and people receiving blessing.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Humility inspires humility and brings a win for everyone. The 920 life: every person in my life is my “2”; I practise the “0” of the self-emptied life; and the result is the “9”—the ninefold fruit of the Spirit. Life first, then relationships, then ministry.
q: Who is God? — God first changed Jacob at the Jabbok and then restored the brothers’ relationship; what does this show you about how God works?
Who am I? — In which relationship are you still “playing tricks” instead of being humble?
How shall I respond? — Towards which of “my 2” will you take one small, humble step?
lessons.jesus: Jesus did not speak coldly to Peter after his fall. Instead he prepared a charcoal fire and breakfast on the shore and asked him three times, “Do you love me?” His gentleness raised up a man who had failed and restored a broken relationship.
lessons.pray: Lord, thank you for changing Jacob first, and for changing me again and again. Take away my heart that plays tricks and meets force with force in relationships, and give me a gentle answer that turns away wrath. Help me, in one difficult relationship, to be the first to bow and the first to lower my head, so that you receive glory and both of us are blessed. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Reach out to someone you have drifted apart from, and send a word of greeting
When someone talks back to you today, answer once in a gentle tone
Write down three things to be thankful for in the “2” you find hardest to get along with
lessons.noon: “A gentle answer turns away wrath.” — Lord, right now let my words carry your gentleness.

lessons.title: Submit and Resist
lessons.theme: Only when we first submit to God can we resist the devil

v: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.
Be sober and self-controlled. Be watchful. Your adversary, the devil, walks around like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour.
Withstand him steadfast in your faith, knowing that your brothers who are in the world are undergoing the same sufferings.

lessons.still: Say quietly, “Lord, I submit to you.” Hand over to him today’s plans, emotions and weaknesses one by one. Then, with a clear mind, declare: “In Christ I do not fear the enemy, because you have already won.”
teach: If a soldier ignores his commander’s orders and charges onto the battlefield on his own, however brave he is, he will only die in vain. Spiritual warfare also has an order: “Be subject to God” comes first, and “resist the devil” comes second. Resistance without submission is just human bravado; with submission, resistance carries authority.

James sets out the order clearly: submit to God, resist the devil, draw near to God. Peter says the devil is like a roaring lion and calls us to be sober and watchful and to resist him, steadfast in faith. Notice that both apostles speak first about humility and then about warfare—“God resists the proud,” “Humble yourselves.” Humility is the very foundation for resisting the devil.

The enemy’s favourite doors are pride, bitterness, unforgiveness and fear. Submitting to God means shutting those doors. Resisting is not a matter of a loud voice or special rituals; it is a matter of truth: like Jesus, answering lies with “It is written,” and drawing near to God, staying in his presence.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let Jesus reign—serve by his authority, and fight by his authority. Self-ruled people want to fight their battles themselves; self-emptied people obey the Commander. Humility overcomes pride; the self-emptied life overcomes Satan—victory lies not in my strength but in my submission.
q: Who is God? — “Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you”: how does this promise help you know God?
Who am I? — Which door in your life may be standing open to the enemy?
How shall I respond? — Which verse will you use today to resist a lie that often troubles you?
lessons.jesus: Jesus fasted forty days and nights in the wilderness and was tempted three times. Each time he answered, “It is written,” and finally said, “Get behind me, Satan!” Because he fully submitted to the Father, he had authority to resist the enemy. This victorious Lord is with us today.
lessons.pray: Lord, I submit to you and hand over to you my thoughts, my emotions and my plans. Shut the doors in my life that stand open to the enemy—pride, bitterness and fear. By your word I resist the devil’s lies. I want to draw near to you, because you have promised to draw near to me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Identify a lie that often troubles you, and write down a verse that answers it
When you are tempted today, first say: “Lord, I submit to you”
lessons.noon: “Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.” — Lord, right now I submit to you and draw near to you.

lessons.title: The Victory of the Self-Emptied Life
lessons.theme: The Lamb’s blood and the self-emptied life overcome the enemy

v: They overcame him because of the Lamb’s blood, and because of the word of their testimony. They didn’t love their life, even to death.
You are of God, little children, and have overcome them, because greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world.

lessons.still: Quietly look up to the Lamb on the cross and say, “Lord, your blood has already won.” Hand your weakness over to him; exchange your fear for trust and your burdens for praise.
teach: In chess, a player sometimes sacrifices a rook and, by doing so, checkmates the opponent’s king. The cross was the most unexpected move in history: the enemy thought he had won by having Jesus crucified, not knowing that the Lamb’s death was his own endgame. God’s victories often come in what looks like defeat.

Revelation says the believers overcame the accuser for three reasons: the Lamb’s blood, the word of their testimony, and not loving their lives even to death. The third is the self-emptied life: no longer centred on self, not clinging even to life itself. All the enemy’s weapons—accusation, intimidation, temptation—are aimed at the “self”; when a person lives the self-emptied life, he finds nothing to grip.

John says, “Greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world.” This week we have seen Satan’s pride, the cycle of pride, the win-win of humility, submitting and resisting, and finally the victory of the self-emptied life. After battle we need rest; next week we will learn to enter God’s rest within the rhythm he has established.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The self-emptied life overcomes Satan; humility overcomes pride. Self-emptying does not mean being nothing; it means entering the infinite and living out the infinite—letting the Greater One live in me. A defeated life becomes an overcoming life, and the key is who reigns.
q: Who is God? — “Greater is he who is in you”: how does this change the way you see your own battles?
Who am I? — Which part of your “self” does the enemy most often target: your pride, your rights, or your comfort?
How shall I respond? — To whom will you testify about something God has done today?
lessons.jesus: On the cross Jesus seemed to be defeated, but in fact he was winning. Paul says that through the cross he triumphed over all rulers and authorities and took them captive. By giving himself up, he overcame the proud enemy. His victory is already complete, and we fight from within his victory.
lessons.pray: Victorious Lamb, thank you for overcoming the enemy by your own blood. Greater is he who is in me than he who is in the world. Free me from the heart that clings to self, so that I do not hold on to my pride, my rights or my comfort, but let you alone live in me. May I stand in your victory every day. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Share with a friend one victory God has won in your life
Today, lay down your rights in one matter and hand it to the Lord
At the weekend, pray together with a spiritual companion for each other’s battles
lessons.noon: “Because greater is he who is in you than he who is in the world.” — Lord, right now I stand in your victory.
